pr_title: LE Audio: LC3 macro hardcode fix
pr_body:
Updates a bunch of LC3 macros from using hardcoded context and location to be more flexible. 

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/43202
pr_comments:
Marking this PR as draft, as I've yet to find a solution to the odd documentation builds error:
```
 Warning, treated as error:
/home/runner/work/zephyr/zephyr/include/zephyr/bluetooth/audio/lc3.h:315: argument 'em' of command @param is not found in the argument list of BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG(_freq, _duration, _loc, _len, _frames_per_sdu, _stream_context)
```
The documentation seems to fail to build HTML due to the `_` prefix in the macro parameters (removing them fixes it). Not quite how to fix that in this PR, without removing the `_` prefix...
Rebased in attempt to fix documentation error

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Avoid hardcoding context type for LC3 macros
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG_*` macros have a hardcoded context type, which doesn't really make any sense. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I see 3 options:
1. The context type should be removed from `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG_*` and thus also from `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG`
2. The context type becomes a parameter to `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG_*`
3. The `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG_*` should be removed and users should use `BT_CODEC_LC3_CONFIG` directly

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
See above

**Additional context**
N/A
comments: Also the LC3 part of the macros should be removed, as they have been "upgraded" to Generic Audio - hence _can_ be used for any codec.

> Also the LC3 part of the macros should be removed, as they have been "upgraded" to Generic Audio - hence _can_ be used for any codec.

Or we need to have a set of generic codec macros, and some specific for LC3 that uses the generic ones by basically just adding the LC3 codec ID

review_comments: I'm not sure it makes sense to have a compile-time defined location. When setting up a stereo stream you typically want to make two different locations - RIGHT to one stream and LEFT to the other - or pack left and right into the same stream.
